title.value: SymmCD: Symmetry-Preserving Crystal Generation with Diffusion Models
title.justification: The title is mentioned at the start of the paper and encapsulates the essence of the research, which centers around a novel approach to crystal generation using diffusion models while preserving symmetry.
title.quote: SymmCD: Symmetry-Preserving Crystal Generation with Diffusion Models

analysis.description: The paper proposes SymmCD, a novel diffusion-based generative model for crystal generation that incorporates crystallographic symmetry explicitly into the generative process. The model decomposes crystals into asymmetric units and symmetry transformations to ensure realistic symmetry and physical properties of the generated crystals.

type.justification: The paper presents an empirical study as it describes the development and experimental evaluation of a novel deep learning model, SymmCD, comparing its performance against existing baselines on crystal generation.
type.quote: We empirically demonstrate our contributions, particularly in ensuring we generate crystals with desired symmetries while being competitive with existing baselines.

name.justification: The research is focused on generating crystalline materials, which is a significant topic within the field of Materials Science.
name.quote: Generating novel crystalline materials has the potential to lead to advancements in fields such as electronics, energy storage, and catalysis.

name.justification: The study of crystal structures and their symmetry is central to this research, addressed within the context of diffusion models for crystal generation.
name.quote: The defining characteristic of crystals is their symmetry, which plays a central role in determining their physical properties.

name.justification: The paper focuses on a novel generative model, SymmCD, for the creation of new crystal structures.
name.quote: In this work, we propose a novel approach for generative modeling of crystals that ensures any desired distribution of space groups.

name.justification: SymmCD is the primary model proposed and developed in the paper. It is a novel generative model designed to preserve symmetry in crystal generation.
name.quote: In this work, we propose a novel approach for generative modeling of crystals that ensures any desired distribution of space groups.

is_contributed.justification: SymmCD is the contribution of this research, aiming to address the limitations of existing crystal generation methods.
is_contributed.quote: We propose SymmCD, a novel diffusion-based generative model that explicitly incorporates crystallographic symmetry into the generative process.

is_executed.justification: The paper details the execution of SymmCD through various experiments and comparison with other models.
is_executed.quote: We empirically demonstrate our contributions, particularly in ensuring we generate crystals with desired symmetries while being competitive with existing baselines.

is_compared.justification: SymmCD is compared with four recent baselines in terms of generating symmetric, stable, and valid crystals.
is_compared.quote: We empirically demonstrate our contributions, particularly in ensuring we generate crystals with desired symmetries while being competitive with existing baselines.

referenced_paper_title.justification: SymmCD is a newly proposed model in this paper, so there is no previous reference paper to cite.

name.justification: DiffCSP is mentioned as one of the models that frequently generates low-symmetry crystal structures.
name.quote: The most frequently generated crystals by DiffCSP (Jiao et al., 2023) and CDVAE (Xie et al., 2022) are in the low-symmetry P1 space group.

is_contributed.justification: DiffCSP is used as a baseline for comparison and is not a contribution of this paper.
is_contributed.quote: We compare our proposed method with four recent strong baselines: CDVAE (Xie et al., 2022), DiffCSP (Jiao et al., 2023), DiffCSP++ (Jiao et al., 2024) and FlowMM (Miller et al., 2024)

is_executed.justification: The paper includes experiments comparing SymmCD with DiffCSP among other models.
is_executed.quote: We compare our proposed method with four recent strong baselines: CDVAE (Xie et al., 2022), DiffCSP (Jiao et al., 2023), DiffCSP++ (Jiao et al., 2024) and FlowMM (Miller et al., 2024)

is_compared.justification: DiffCSP is one of the baselines used for comparison with SymmCD in the experiments conducted.
is_compared.quote: We empirically demonstrate our contributions, particularly in ensuring we generate crystals with desired symmetries while being competitive with existing baselines.

referenced_paper_title.value: Crystal structure prediction by joint equivariant diffusion
referenced_paper_title.justification: This is the reference paper for DiffCSP, as the citation of Jiao et al., 2023 matches this title.
referenced_paper_title.quote: DiffCSP and FlowMM generate many crystals with low symmetry and generally have lower diversity of space groups.

name.justification: The MP-20 dataset, a subset of the Materials Project, is used to train and evaluate SymmCD.
name.quote: We test our model on de novo crystal generation using the MP-20 dataset (Xie et al., 2022), a subset of the Materials Project (Jain et al., 2013).

name.justification: Pymatgen is used in the paper to find space groups of generated structures.
name.quote: To detect the space group of the generated structures, we use spglib’s symmetry finding method (Togo and Tanaka, 2018b; Ong et al., 2013) with a tolerance of 0.1Å.
